correctness.rationale: For \(\Omega(n)\le2\), the three possible shapes are prime, prime square, and distinct-prime semiprime. Direct substitution gives the prime and quadratic branches. The semiprime equation is algebraically equivalent to \(((a-b)p-b)((a-b)q-b)=ab-(a-b)k\). If the right side vanishes, coprimality forces \(a-b=1\) and the vanishing factor to be the prime \(b\), yielding exactly \((a,b,k)=(r+1,r,r(r+1))\); the prime and square branches are then absent. Every step is reversible, and bounded exact-arithmetic regression checks found no mismatch.

value.rationale: The claim gives a natural complete classification of the first nontrivial multiplicative layer of a central divisor-sum Diophantine equation and isolates the exact parameter locus where that layer changes from finite to infinite. The result is structural rather than a bounded table: it converts all distinct-prime solutions to divisor pairs of one explicit constant and exactly identifies the regular prime-base family when that constant vanishes.
